mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates economic expansion, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but SPX returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 7% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and equity markets.
failure_condition: UNRATE below 7% but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in unemployment and payroll employment signals strong economic health, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Both UNRATE and PAYEMS improve but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate in a tightening cycle may lead to decreased borrowing and negative equity returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS above 4% but SPX returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests accommodative monetary policy, supporting higher equity valuations.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL growth is low but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth above 98 indicates strong supply activity, leading to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO above 98 but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales (RSAFS) and employment (PAYEMS) together indicate strong demand, boosting equity markets.
failure_condition: RSAFS and PAYEMS both rise but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) above 600 in late-cycle expansion may signal overbuilding, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: HOUST above 600 but SPX returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
